Sophie (New Hire): Hey @people-ops — quick Q about my H-4 -> H-1 COS. Offer shows start date 2026-06-01 but the attorney says USCIS may take longer. If COS approval comes after 6/1, can payroll/benefits start earlier (receipt exists) or do we need to push the official start? :thinking:
Aisha (People Ops): Congrats Sophie! Short answer: we need active work authorization to put you on payroll. For H-1 COS you are only authorized once USCIS approves and the start date on the approval arrives. Receipt alone doesn't allow employment. We can either set you to an unpaid onboarding status on 6/1 or move the official paid start. Can you share the receipt number and upload docs to Workday?
Sophie (New Hire): Receipt is WAC-22-12345678. No prior EAD. Uploading passport/I-94 now.
Ben (Hiring Manager): Sophie — we really want you on the team starting 6/1. Is unpaid remote onboarding an option (team intros, docs) until authorization?
Aisha (People Ops): Yes, unpaid onboarding is possible. Note: benefits (medical/dental/401k) generally require an active paid employee status. Some vendors will allow exceptions or retroactive effective dates if we provide immigration documentation. We'll coordinate with benefits.
Raj (Payroll): FYI payroll needs either an I-9 showing current authorization or completion of Section 1 with Section 2 after authorization. For COS cases we typically complete Section 1 and wait to complete Section 2 until you have the approval notice or H-1 visa stamp. If Sophie is unpaid we flag as 'onboarding — not on payroll' so no salary or benefit enrollment triggers. We can retro-pay from the approved start date if desired. @Immigration Legal — please confirm.
Immigration Legal: Confirming — change of status does NOT authorize employment until USCIS approval and the start date on the approval (or you enter the US in H-1 status via stamping). Receipt doesn't permit work. If there's an RFE or significant delay, we should discuss adjusting the start date or unpaid onboarding in writing.
Sophie (New Hire): Understood. One concern: I need health coverage starting June because of ongoing prescriptions. If my paid start is delayed, can benefits be backdated or can an exception be made?
Aisha (People Ops): We can request a special enrollment exception with the benefits vendor citing immigration processing. Please email benefits@redwood.com with your case receipt and proposed start date and I'll attach supporting docs. In some cases they can make the medical effective date align with your paid start or allow a retroactive enrollment.
Sophie (New Hire): Sending the note now. Thanks.
onboarding-bot: Reminder: please upload passport, I-94, and offer acceptance to Workday: https://workday.redwood.com/onboarding (internal).
Raj (Payroll): Also note: tax withholding and 401(k) eligibility start when payroll begins. If we retro-pay, taxes will be applied in that pay period and 401(k) match can be applied retroactively depending on plan rules. Let us know preferred pay method and if you need direct deposit set up early.
Ben (Hiring Manager): We'll do unpaid orientation sessions (no prod access) so Sophie can hit the ground running once cleared.
Sophie (New Hire): Appreciate the flexibility. One last thing — if approval comes but the effective H-1 start date on the approval is later than offer date, can we set my payroll start to the approval start and still get employer match for 401k?
Aisha (People Ops): Usually match is governed by plan eligibility periods. If your paid service date is effectively the approval start, match eligibility follows that. We can work with Benefits to preserve match if retro-pay is processed. I'll follow up with the benefits rep.
Immigration Legal: If processing extends beyond 90 days after the offered start, escalate to legal/people ops to decide on formal start adjustment. Also avoid any work in the US until authorized.
Sophie (New Hire): Thanks everyone — I'll keep you posted on any USCIS updates. :pray:
